entities.summary: Portuguese Plain Style architecture refers to a 16th century Portuguese architectural style related to early Mannerism marked by austerity and sobriety of form. The term was coined by the American art historian George Kubler, who defines this style as "vernacular architecture, related to the traditions of a living dialect more than to the great authors of Classical Antiquity". This same author traces the origin of this style back to suggestions by Italian military architects, although there may be influences from Northern Europe and from the Portuguese architectural tradition itself.
